description: Evaluation benchmarks for the WTF (Walk Through Foundations) skill, verifying visual graphs, progressive pacing, audience calibration, and active checks.

evals.name: db-index-fundamentals
assertions: Provides a 3-4 step roadmap before deep diving
Includes a visual diagram (Mermaid flowchart or ASCII tree) illustrating B-Tree search
Uses an intuitive physical analogy (e.g. alphabetized book, library catalog)
Ends Piece 1 with an active micro-check question and pauses for user response

evals.name: git-rebase-vs-merge
evals.prompt: wtf is git rebase and why do seniors love it so much?
assertions: Outlines a concise piece-by-piece learning roadmap
Includes a git branch/commit graph showing replay of commits onto a new base
Clarifies that commit SHAs change during rebase
Concludes the first piece with a thought experiment regarding public branches

evals.name: kafka-streaming-eli5
evals.prompt: wtf is Apache Kafka explain like I am 10
assertions: Uses child-accessible physical metaphor (conveyor belt, notebook, post office)
Zero impenetrable jargon (no unexplained zookeeper/kraft/broker terminology)
Includes a clear visual diagram showing producer -> log -> consumer
Presents an active check checking understanding of the conveyor belt

evals.name: event-loop-javascript
evals.prompt: /wtf is the JavaScript event loop? why doesn't setTimeout(fn, 0) run immediately?
assertions: Breaks down Call Stack, Web APIs, and Task Queue in a clear roadmap
Features a visual sequence or flow diagram showing queue ordering
Tests mental model with a predict-the-console-output micro-puzzle
